clue.text: It can be made up into a suit, though it's a job

indicators.note: cloth is made up into a garment, so these words are reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: all nine letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A tailor's remark that some fabric can be made into a suit, though it is quite a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into a suit' looks like the destination of the making up; it is the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a post or position of employment, as in 'situations vacant' advertisements.

clue.text: What's going round the Southeast about a report, it appears

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the compass points sit on either side of what follows

parts.note: S and E, the compass abbreviations for south and east
taken as written
to tell is to report or relate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rumour circulating in the south-east of England, reported in the local news.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points are separate letters at either end, not a region; they wrap the rest of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a body or craft that travels in orbit around a planet.

clue.text: Set up thus in play or opera

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up turns it to read from the bottom
in places one word inside the other

parts.note: to act is to play a part
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A director staging something in this way, whether a play or an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' covers the whole insertion, which is then read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is Puccini's opera about the singer Floria Tosca, first staged in Rome in 1900.

clue.text: Area must appear replanned by non-professional people

indicators.note: something replanned is laid out afresh, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A district that, it seems, must be redesigned by people without professional training.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurs do something for pleasure rather than payment, the opposite of professionals.

clue.text: Thought to have some inclination for a perfectionist

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a ship has a list when it leans to one side

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a perfectionist is thought to have some leaning.
explanation.walkthrough: Inclination here is the nautical lean of a ship, not a preference.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist holds to lofty standards and pursues perfection, so the two words describe similar temperaments.

clue.text: Almost never but not always before time

indicators.note: but not means except, so one word is taken away from the other

parts.note: taken as written
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
early means ahead of the appointed time

explanation.surface: A wry remark about something that almost never happens, though not always, ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 'always' away from 'never' leaves a single letter; the leftover N is what the surface's paradox hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost are interchangeable adverbs meaning very close to but not quite.

clue.text: A good deal makes sense

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one of the five senses, vision

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a shrewd bargain being sensible; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally 'a sight' means a great deal, and the same word names the faculty of vision.

clue.text: Understand a proverb can divert youngsters

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun for it

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in 'I see'
a saw is an old saying

explanation.surface: Grasping that a wise saying can entertain children.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw is an old word for a proverb, as in 'an old saw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a playground plank on which two children bob up and down, amusing them.

clue.text: Gold tiara made by an old fighting man

indicators.note: made means fashioned or crafted, so these letters are worked into something new

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A golden crown crafted by an ancient warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiators were armed combatants who fought in Roman arenas for public entertainment.

clue.text: Seen in the enchantress's hair

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the last five letters of the word, before the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Something glimpsed in a sorceress's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of a person's hair, usually a woman's.

clue.text: Willing to write a half-term exam in advance

indicators.note: in advance puts one piece in front of the rest

parts.note: a test is an exam
taken as written

indicators.note: half means only part of the word is kept, its opening two letters

parts.note: the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A pupil keen to sit an exam early, half-way through the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' is read as 'having made a will'; the exam is written ahead of A and TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate is the legal term for someone who has died leaving a valid will, so 'willing' is a pun.

clue.text: The usual hail-storm

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting, as in 'Ave Maria'
to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: A hailstorm as everyday weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Hail is a greeting, not ice; storm is an outburst of anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Average describes the ordinary, typical or normal standard of something.

clue.text: Don't take time off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to let something remain where it is
second meaning: a period of permitted absence from work

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a boss refusing a holiday; the halves are two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to let something stay behind, and the noun is authorised absence from duty.

clue.text: A bull maybe is recumbent outside — result of these tranquillizers?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the words are only one possible arrangement of their letters
outside puts one piece around the other

parts.note: something recumbent lies down
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A bull lying down, soothed into rest by songs.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged A BULL sits inside LIES; the surface then jokes that the bull lies down because of these songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lullabies are soothing songs sung to calm a baby into sleep, so they act as gentle sedatives.

clue.text: Principal source of this concern

definitions.note: a cryptic description rather than a plain synonym
definitions.meaning: first meaning: money earned on a capital sum, the principal
second meaning: a stake or share in something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like 'main', but it is the capital sum on which a bank pays out.
explanation.definitionFit: Money lent as principal yields a percentage return, and a concern or stake in a business is also called an interest.

clue.text: Conservative holding all the way? It's hardly credible

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
taken as written
ST, short for street, a common crossword way

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician sticking to the party line all the way, and nobody believing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an exaggerated, implausible tale that listeners are unlikely to believe.

clue.text: To agitate could mean prison!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to mix or ... up trouble

explanation.walkthrough: The surface warns that agitating could land you in jail; stir is old slang for a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to agitate a liquid or a crowd, and in slang the same word means a jail.

clue.text: Stand for an army corps here

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a person who is here is present

explanation.surface: Someone offering to stand in for an army corps that is here.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to symbolise or act on its behalf, which is what standing for it means.

clue.text: Bun well-cooked taken as nourishment — there's nothing better

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer rather than an adjective

indicators.note: something well-cooked has been thoroughly worked over, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: these three letters rearranged
food taken as nourishment has been eaten

explanation.surface: A well-baked bun, eaten for sustenance, is the best thing going.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbeaten has never been defeated, so no rival has proved superior to it.

clue.text: Put on airs about French article on English ballet

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the last piece goes underneath
about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to swank is to show off
la is French for 'the'
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone showing off about a French piece of writing on an English ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on airs' is a single verb for showing off; 'article' is the grammatical kind, not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake is Tchaikovsky's famous ballet about a princess turned into a swan.

clue.text: Everything turned on the egghead woman

indicators.note: on means attached after, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: the head of egg, its opening letter

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Everything depends on an intellectual woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like one word for a brainy person, but it splits into egg and head.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a woman's first name, as in the jazz singer Ella Fitzgerald.

clue.text: Plant about a quarter before the fall to get early blossom

indicators.note: before puts this part ahead of the next
about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to sow seed is to plant it
N, north, one of the four compass quarters
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: put bulbs in a few months before autumn to have flowers early in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fall' suggests the American autumn, but it is just a drop. N sits inside SOW.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowdrop is a small white flower that blooms in late winter, among the first of the year.

clue.text: His merchandise is measured by the foot

definitions.text: His merchandise is measured by the foot

parts.words: His merchandise is measured by the foot
parts.note: surface reading: a trader selling cloth or rope by length, in units of twelve inches
setter's reading: the goods are socks and stockings, sized to fit the wearer's foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'By the foot' sounds like a unit of length, but it means the part of the body the goods are fitted to.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosier sells socks and stockings, which come in sizes matched to the customer's feet.

clue.text: Quick-witted statesman

definitions.meaning: second meaning: John ..., the Victorian Liberal politician and free-trade campaigner

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one clever politician; the halves are separate. John Bright was a 19th-century British radical MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever person is called bright, and John Bright was a celebrated Victorian parliamentarian.

clue.text: "A beast, that wants of reason" (Hamlet)

definitions.note: a quotation with a word missing, which the answer supplies

parts.note: surface reading: a line about an animal that has no reason
setter's reading: the full line in Hamlet's first soliloquy has a missing word before 'of reason'

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet says 'a beast, that wants discourse of reason, would have mourn'd longer'; the clue drops that word. 'Wants' means lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's line the missing noun means the faculty of rational thought, the power of reasoning.

clue.text: Baboon's army training?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a West African baboon species, close relative of the mandrill
second meaning: marching practice on the parade ground

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an ape doing military exercises; the apostrophe-s is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The drill is a West African primate, and soldiers practise marching and weapons handling in drill.

clue.text: One lacking nothing holds a few, being quite unaffected

indicators.note: holds means keeps inside, so one piece goes within the other
lacking means going without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
O, the zero shape
taken as written
a loose use: four, a small number, in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A person with nothing holds onto a little and stays perfectly natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Few' standing for a specific number is unusually loose; the four letters needed inside are A and the Roman four, which a few can stretch to mean.
explanation.definitionFit: A naive person is innocent and artless, without pretence or sophistication.

clue.text: Cross one with speed

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals
rate means speed, as in 'at a fast rate'

explanation.surface: Getting angry while driving fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb, as in crossing a road; it is the adjective for angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate and cross are both adjectives meaning angry or annoyed.

clue.text: Press job

parts.note: surface reading: a post in journalism, working for the newspapers
setter's reading: press means flattening clothes with a hot appliance, a household chore

explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' suggests newspapers; here it is smoothing creases out of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes with a hot flat appliance to remove creases is the household chore in question.

clue.text: Bill's entering the wood bearing food

indicators.note: bearing means carrying along, so an extra letter is attached at the end
entering means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: teak is a hardwood
AC, short for account, which is a bill
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Bill walks into the woods carrying something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' does double duty: it signals carrying and it is the compass point E.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacake is a toasted, buttered sweet bun with currants, eaten with tea.

clue.text: A course for the egg-producer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single row of bricks or stones in a wall
second meaning: a hen that lays

explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a dish on a menu, which suits the egg; it is a bricklayer's row.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer is one level or stratum, such as a course of bricks, and also a hen kept for laying.

clue.text: One finishing in the trial is the most vulnerable

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a test is a trial
one who finishes something is an ender

explanation.surface: The competitor finishing the trial is the weakest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means sensitive or easily hurt, and the superlative form means the most easily hurt.
